title: Material resource_name is not preserved during GLTF export
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.4.1, 4.5 and current master branch.

### System information

(system is irrelevant for this)

### Issue description

When exporting a GLTF model from a Godot scene using `GLTFDocument` and `GLTFState`, the `resource_name` given to the materials may not be preserved if it contains certain symbols, as they are subjected to a `String.validate_node_name()` check during the export process.

Since resources are not nodes, this check seems out of place to me -- as far as I can tell, `resource_name` is just a mere string within the Resource data, so I don't suppose it needs to be sanitized -- and indeed this validation check is not enforced during import, only during export. And since the materials are also being exported, it also seems unnecessary, as the material names are no longer Godot's concern once they're exported.

In my particular use case I would actually need them to be preserved as they are, as I'm trying to work with the map editor NetRadiant Custom, which, in order to display the models correctly, it requires the material name to be the path to the texture used by each model. (I export models for it (using a tool script) so I can scale them and adjust them to the editor's coordinate system. I created some inherited scenes, and I'm exporting GLTFs from them.)

So the material names I export from Blender look like `"textures/models/vehicles/car3_green"`. Godot imports those names just fine and puts them in the materials' `resource_name`. But then when I try to export the inherited scenes, the export process does the `String.validate_node_name()` check, which doesn't allow the `/` symbols and converts them to underscores, and then NetRadiant can't find the textures.

The problem is in `GLTFDocument::_serialize_materials`. 
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/55457bd95a41b5a0d3625ac39cf296b3b657defd/modules/gltf/gltf_document.cpp#L4491-L4493

It calls `_gen_unique_name`, which redirects to `_gen_unique_name_static`, which in turn does the node name check.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/55457bd95a41b5a0d3625ac39cf296b3b657defd/modules/gltf/gltf_document.cpp#L9027-L9028


### Steps to reproduce

1. export a gltf model from Blender, with materials, and with material names that contain `/` or any symbols that are illegal for node names.
2. import model into Godot, create an inherited scene and check in the inspector that the mesh's material name in its `Resource -> Name` (the `resource_name` property) is the same as in Blender. 
3. Use a tool EditorScript to export that scene as another gltf. 
4. observe in the gltf file that the material name is now using underscores where it used to have those "illegal" symbols (search for "materials" to find it). Or alternatively, intercept the export code with a `GLTFDocumentExtension`, and in `_export_post(state: GLTFState)` check the `state.json.materials[0].name` property, which has already been changed at that point.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

I haven't created one. I may create one when I have more free time, unless it deemed unnecessary. Please let me know.
